author: EmuCore - Hub
title: From catalog tap to verified install: EmuCoreX's texture-pack pipeline
summary: Large replacement packs need more than a progress bar. EmuCoreX gives every transfer a persistent identity, resumes partial payloads with HTTP ranges, verifies declared sizes and SHA-256 hashes, and installs only after the complete archive passes those checks.
heroAlt: A texture-rendering example stored in the SDL source included with EmuCoreX

blocks.text: A queue entry survives the screen that created it

`TextureDownloadManager.enqueue()` first checks that the catalog pack declares compatibility with the selected game serial. `TextureDownloadStore` then derives a 32-character key from the pack and serial, writes task state under `noBackupFilesDir/texture-downloads`, and hands a uniquely named job to Android `WorkManager`. Closing the texture catalog does not make that job anonymous: queued, downloading, paused, waiting, verifying, installing, completed, failed, and cancelled states remain available to the UI.
Resume is negotiated with the server, not assumed

The worker measures the existing partial file and sends an HTTP `Range` request when an offset is available. It appends only after receiving a partial response whose `Content-Range` starts at exactly that byte. If the server ignores the range, the worker deletes the old fragment and restarts from zero; if the range is inconsistent, it rejects the response. Connections are HTTPS-only, redirects are followed manually for at most eight hops, and a redirect may not downgrade the transfer to HTTP.

The rotating-texture example comes from the SDL tree carried in EmuCoreX. The download pipeline supplies replacement image data; the renderer remains responsible for turning verified content into live textures.
Progress is computed from bytes that are already on disk

Each chunk is written through `RandomAccessFile`, while samples taken roughly every 750 milliseconds feed downloaded bytes, a smoothed byte rate, and an estimated remaining time into both WorkManager progress and a foreground notification. Pause cancels the unique worker but retains its payload. Resume re-reads the partial length before scheduling replacement work. Cancel marks the task, stops its worker, and discards payload files, which gives pause and cancel intentionally different storage semantics.
Multipart packs are verified twice before assembly is trusted

The July 27 multipart change lets a catalog entry list several `RemoteTexturePart` records. Each part has its own URL, byte count, and SHA-256 digest. The worker downloads them in order, checks the size and digest of every part while copying them into one archive, and simultaneously computes a digest for the assembled stream. The final byte count and whole-pack SHA-256 must also match the catalog. An incomplete list, oversized response, altered part, or corrupt final archive ends the pipeline before installation.
Installation is a separate state with explicit consequences

Only after verification does the task enter `INSTALLING` and call `TexturePackRepository.installRemotePack()` for the selected serial. A successful install updates `RemoteContentInstallState`, enables texture replacements in `AppPreferences`, removes temporary payloads, and marks the task complete. Network exceptions instead move a running job to `WAITING_NETWORK` and ask WorkManager for an exponential-backoff retry; catalog or integrity errors are treated as permanent failures rather than endless retries.

Archive extraction is also bounded. The July 28 follow-up raised the texture extraction ceiling to 12 GiB for genuinely large packs, but retained a finite limit so compressed input cannot expand without control.
